$comment: The APPLICATION project: everything that runs in a browser, plus the unit tests.
noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature is deliberately OFF here and ON in the tooling project:
vite/client types a CSS Module as { readonly [k: string]: string }, so the flag would force
styles['failureTitle'] on every className in the workspace. That is a real cost paid by ten
workers for no safety — a missing class name is a styling defect, never an evidentiary one.
Tooling (vite/vitest config, scripts/, the Playwright specs) lives in tsconfig.node.json,
which is the only project that may see @types/node. The application must not be able to
reach a Node global by accident.
docs/leads/ui.md D1 pins TypeScript 5.9.x with strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess +
exactOptionalPropertyTypes. erasableSyntaxOnly is added on top so that no file in this
workspace can use a construct (enum, namespace, parameter property) that Node's built-in
type stripping cannot run — scripts/*.ts are executed by `node` directly, with no bundler.
